lesson.text: Quick memory: what is a bug? (A mistake in a program.) Today: how to start a big job.
Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller parts. Each small part is easier to understand and to solve.
Building a castle in the game? Its parts: the walls, the towers, the gate and the roof. Build each part, and the castle is done.
You can break a part into even smaller parts: the gate becomes the frame, the door and the torches beside it.
Programmers do the same: a game has parts for moving, scoring, sounds and pictures, and different people can work on different parts.
For the robot: first the way to the gem, then the way from the gem to the flag. Two small programs make one big one.
Try it in the world: pick a big build, like a farm. Write its parts (fence, field, water, animals, barn), then build one part at a time.

choices: breaking a big problem into smaller parts
exercises.explain: Decomposition is breaking a big problem into smaller parts that are easier to solve.

exercises.prompt: A small part of a problem is usually easier to solve than the whole problem.
exercises.hint: Is one wall easier than a whole castle?
exercises.explain: True: small parts are easier to understand and to solve.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are parts of building a treehouse?
exercises.hint: Would you need it to finish the treehouse?
exercises.explain: Parts of the job: the floor, the ladder, the roof, the walls. Brushing teeth and a swimming lesson are not.

exercises.prompt: Which is a sensible small part of the job “plan a picnic”?
exercises.hint: Which one helps the picnic happen?
exercises.explain: Choosing the food is one small part of planning a picnic.

exercises.prompt: Two parts: go to the gem, then go on to the flag. Write the program.
exercises.hint: Plan the first part to the gem. Then plan the second part, from the gem to the flag.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD 4, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 4.

exercises.prompt: Break “make a sandwich” into parts, and put them in order.
exercises.hint: What do you need before you can spread anything?
items: Get the bread and the filling
exercises.explain: Get what you need, spread the butter, add the filling, then put the top slice on.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of a game to its job.
exercises.hint: Think of what each part does while you play.
exercises.explain: Controls move your player, the score counts points, the sounds play music and effects, the map shows where you are.

exercises.prompt: Zara wants to build a whole village. What is the best first step?
exercises.hint: Big jobs start with a plan of the small parts.
choices: list the parts: houses, paths, a well, a farm
build the biggest house without a plan
give up: it is too big
exercises.explain: List the parts first. Then she can build them one at a time.

exercises.prompt: Different people can work on different parts of a big program at the same time.
exercises.hint: Could one friend build walls while another builds the roof?
exercises.explain: True: splitting a big program into parts lets a team work on them at the same time.

exercises.prompt: A castle has 4 towers. Each tower needs 3 parts: a base, a wall and a roof. How many parts is that?
exercises.hint: Work out the parts for one tower, then for all of them.
exercises.explain: Each tower has 3 parts, so 4 × 3 = 12 parts.

exercises.prompt: Break it into parts: pick up both gems, then go to the flag.
exercises.hint: One gem at a time: plan the way to the first gem, then the next, then the flag.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD 2, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 2, TURN LEFT, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 4, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 2.

exercises.prompt: Put these parts of building a house in the game in a sensible order.
exercises.hint: What does each part need to be there already?
items: Build the walls and the door
exercises.explain: Clear the ground, lay the floor, build the walls, put the roof on, then add the lights inside.

exercises.prompt: “Tidy your room” feels too big. Which is the best way to break it up?
choices: put away toys, then books, then clothes
exercises.explain: Toys, then books, then clothes: three small jobs are easier than one big one.

exercises.prompt: A game needs a character that jumps. Which is a smaller part of that job?
exercises.hint: Which one is about the jump itself?
choices: make the character go up, then come back down
exercises.explain: A jump is two small parts: going up, then coming back down.

exercises.prompt: When you break a problem into parts, the order you do them in never matters.
exercises.hint: Can you put the roof on before the walls?
exercises.explain: False: some parts need others first: the walls before the roof, the floor before the furniture.

exercises.prompt: Match each big job to one of its small parts.
matches: draw a picture on the front
exercises.hint: Ask: which small job belongs to this big job?
exercises.explain: Card: draw the front. Garden: plant the seeds. Story: choose the characters. Cake: mix the flour and eggs.

exercises.prompt: Go round the walls, pick up the gem and reach the flag. Plan it in parts!
exercises.hint: Part 1: reach the gem. Part 2: go from the gem to the flag. Then join the parts.
exercises.explain: One program that works: FORWARD, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD 2, TURN RIGHT, FORWARD, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 2, TURN LEFT, FORWARD 3.
